html:
The Great Pyramid of Giza is the tomb of the Egyptian king Khufu, built around 2560 BCE at Giza near modern Cairo. It is the largest of the Egyptian pyramids and the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and the only one still standing.

It was built in the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom, over roughly twenty years or more. When finished it stood about 146 metres tall, and it stayed the tallest building on earth for some 3,800 years, until the spire of Lincoln Cathedral in England passed it in the fourteenth century.

  • It is made of more than two million blocks of limestone and granite.
  • It was covered in smooth white limestone that shone in the sun. Most of that casing was stripped in the Middle Ages to build Cairo.
  • Inside are the King's Chamber, with a granite sarcophagus, and the tall Grand Gallery.

It was not built by slaves, as once thought. Archaeologists have found the town where paid workers lived, ate bread and beer and were buried with honour. Papyri found in 2013, the Diary of Merer, record a team shipping limestone blocks down the Nile to the site.

The pyramid was the peak of a quick burst of learning: Khufu's father Sneferu had built three pyramids, working out the angles by trial. It is part of the Giza pyramid complex, with the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure and the Great Sphinx.
